title: Console UI: route + model usage insights breakdown table (filters, drilldowns, states)
creator: Dylan Brooks
description:
Implement the primary Usage Insights breakdown table UI in Redwood Console for the beta: cost/usage breakdown by API route + model.

Scope (this ticket)
- New page/section under Usage/Cost: “Usage Insights (Beta)” → “Breakdown” view.
- Table component wiring to Insights Query API (ENG-3814) with server-side sorting + pagination.
- Filters (sync to URL/query string): time range, workspace/project, environment, deployment mode (if present), region (if present), route, model.
- Drilldown navigation: click row to open detail view (route+model) and preserve filters on back.
- Loading, empty, error, and partial-data states (incl. data freshness banner from ENG-3824).

Non-goals
- Export CSV job flow (ENG-3816) beyond placing the CTA stub/disabled state.
- “Top cost drivers / what changed” cards (ENG-3819). This view is only the breakdown table.

Key UX behavior
- Default grouping: Route (normalized) + Model (bucketed) rows.
- Default sort: Cost desc.
- Pagination: 50 rows/page (aligned with API default), with “Show 25/50/100” selector if feasible.
- Route display:
  - Prefer human-readable display name (e.g., “Chat Completions”) with route path shown secondary (e.g., “/v1/chat/completions”).
  - If route is “(unattributed)” or “unknown”, show tooltip explaining route tags missing/late.
- Model display:
  - Show model family + version bucket (e.g., “llama-3.1-70b (2026-01 bucket)”) and alias if applicable.

Columns (beta)
- Cost (USD) (primary)
- Requests
- Input tokens
- Output tokens
- Cache hit rate (or hit tokens / total tokens if that’s what API returns)
- Retries (count)
- Fallbacks (count)
- p95 latency (ms)

If API doesn’t have a column yet, render “—” with tooltip “Not available in this release” rather than hiding the column (keeps table stable for beta).

States
- Loading: show skeleton table (header + ~10 rows) and keep filter bar interactive.
- Empty state:
  - If no data for selected time range: “No usage found for this selection.” Provide quick actions: reset filters; set time range to Last 24 hours; link to docs.
  - If user lacks permissions to view cost: show permission-denied state (copy per DES-914), hide cost column values.
- Error state:
  - Network/API failure: show inline callout with request ID (from response headers if available), “Retry” button, and a link to status/support.
  - Query-too-expensive/timeouts: show “This query is too large for interactive view” guidance (suggest shorter range, fewer filters). (Matches support feedback from early perf issues.)
- Partial data / freshness:
  - If API returns lag > threshold: show banner “Data may be delayed by ~X min” and timestamp.

Performance considerations
- Debounce filter changes that trigger queries (300–500ms) except time range apply button.
- Avoid rerendering full table on column resize / hover; virtualize only if necessary (target < 200 rows).
- Cache identical queries in the frontend for quick back/forward navigation (keyed by URL params).

Analytics (Console)
- Emit events:
  - usage_insights.breakdown_viewed
  - usage_insights.breakdown_row_clicked
  - usage_insights.filter_changed (include which filter, not values)
  - usage_insights.error_shown (category)

Acceptance criteria
- Filters are reflected in URL and persist on refresh.
- Table correctly renders API pagination totals and “showing X–Y of Z”.
- Sorting works for cost, requests, tokens, latency.
- Drilldown preserves previous filters and returns to same scroll position (best-effort).
- Loading/empty/error/partial states match UX spec and are keyboard accessible.
- Totals in table match API (no client-side recompute except formatting).

Testing
- Unit tests: filter → query param serialization; column formatting; error mapping.
- E2E (Playwright): load page, apply filters, paginate, click row drilldown, simulate 403, simulate lag banner.

Notes
- Use existing Console table primitives (DataTable v3) and filter bar components.
- Follow terminology guidance from DevEx: prefer “Endpoint” in user-facing copy but keep “Route” in technical contexts/tooltips.

Links
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/in-console-usage-insights-prd.json
- UX spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/usage-insights-console-ux-spec.json
- API contract: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/usage-insights-api-contract.json
